messages:
maria: heads up — PR #6721 (kv-cache: smarter eviction window) is ready for final review. It improves cache hit rate but I saw a small tail-latency bump in the long-seq bench. need a merge window slot.

sam: pinging for reviews. I skimmed the code — looks fine but want a bench run with canary config. did you run against 1k/2k seq?

maria: ran standard long-seq sweep: 512, 1024, 2048. attaching quick numbers below. baseline = current main, branch = pr-6721.

maria: ```
cmd: bench/run_longseq.sh --model=gpt-small --concurrency=64 --seqs="512,1024,2048"
baseline tail p99: 112ms
branch tail p99: 134ms (+20%)
baseline median: 18ms
branch median: 20ms (+11%)
throughput (tokens/s): baseline 10.3k, branch 10.1k (-1.9%)
mem per shard: baseline 6.2GB, branch 6.4GB (+3%)
```

lee: thanks. that p99 delta is concerning. do you have the breakdown by request size? could be an allocation spike at big seqs.

maria: breakdown by seq: 512 p99 +6%, 1024 p99 +14%, 2048 p99 +32%. looks like larger sequences amplify the tail.

ash: cc @sam @lee — is this acceptable given the hit-rate win? what's the hit-rate improvement numbers?

maria: hit-rate: baseline 48%, branch 62% (+14pp). per-token cost down ~6% in simulated traffic. tradeoff seems cost vs tail for long sequences.

sam: wondering if we can gate the new eviction policy behind a routing flag for long-seq heavy routes. that would let us enable broadly but avoid regressions for latency-sensitive flows.

maria: good call. PR already adds a config flag: kv.eviction.policy=adaptive and kv.eviction.long_seq_threshold=1500. default is off. I tested with flag on/off.

jordan: is there a canary job configured to exercise long sequences? if not we should run one before merging.

maria: not yet, I can trigger a canary: /canary run pr-6721 longseq-64c. results should be in ~30m.

deploy-bot: Canary started for pr-6721 on cluster-us-east-1 (canary-id: cny-9812). Status: running.

lee: if canary is clean for 30m across seq distributions and no OOMs, i'm happy to approve with a note to watch p99 dashboards after merge.

sam: i'll do a quick code review pass now, listing a couple nits but nothing blocking. maria — can you add a short eval note summarizing the hit-rate vs tail trade for the release notes?

maria: will do. adding to PR description and release note draft. also adding rollout plan: 1) enable flag by default in blue environment, 2) monitor p99 and cost; 3) flip in green if stable; 4) rollback config if p99 +15% at global level.

ash: +1 to rollout. also request we schedule the merge during the low-traffic window tomorrow 09:00–10:00 PST. avoids peak.

jordan: canary finished: deploy-bot link: https://internal/ci/canary/cny-9812 (summary attached). no OOMs, minor p99 blip at 2048 but within expected.

deploy-bot: Canary cny-9812 completed: success. metrics: p99 delta at 2048 = +28% but traffic-weighted p99 = +7%.

sam: LGTM from me. leaving formal approve on PR.

lee: approved.

maria: thanks all. scheduling merge for tomorrow 09:15 PST in the low-traffic window. will monitor dashboards and keep rollback plan ready. :thumbsup:
